page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.sn1.medium is an x86_64 cloud server powered by a 2.5 GHz Intel Xeon 8269CY processor. It features 1 physical CPU core with hyper-threading enabled, providing 2 dedicated vCPUs alongside 4.0 GB of memory (2.0 GB per core). The CPU cache architecture includes 32 KB of L1d cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 35 MB of shared L3 cache. Instruction set extensions include AVX, AVX-512F, AES, BMI2, ADX, and FMA. This instance does not include bundled local SSD storage or GPU acceleration, and operates under KVM hypervisor virtualization.

In performance benchmarks, the instance demonstrates baseline execution capabilities. Synthetic testing shows single-core CPU performance in the lower 25th percentile with a stress-ng score of 1097.68, and multi-core CPU performance in the bottom 10th percentile with a stress-ng score of 1455.38. Memory read and write bandwidth tests for uncached large blocks peak at 10.27 GB/sec and 9.34 GB/sec respectively, placing memory throughput in the lower tier. Application-level benchmarks reflect similar results, with PassMark CPU scoring 1824.84, Redis SET throughput reaching 1.42 million operations per second, and static web serving throughput measuring 1.25 GB/sec.

Given its 1:2 memory-to-vCPU ratio and entry-level hardware allocation, the server is suitable for lightweight compute tasks, small-scale web microservices, basic background processing, and development or testing environments. The dedicated vCPU allocation provides predictable performance without burst credit restrictions, making it a low-capacity option for consistent, low-throughput entry-level workloads.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.sn1.medium is an entry-level x86_64 cloud server powered by an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor operating at 2.5 GHz. Configured with 1 physical core and 2 vCPUs via hyper-threading, it provides 4.0 GB of RAM, yielding a 1:2 memory-to-vCPU allocation. The processor features 35 MB of L3 cache along with instruction support for AVX, AVX-512F, and AES encryption. This instance features dedicated CPU resource allocation, operates without bundled local SSD storage or GPU accelerators, and relies on attached network volumes. Across benchmark evaluations, including stress-ng, Geekbench, and PassMark, the server exhibits baseline performance metrics within the lower percentiles for both single-core and multi-core execution. Memory bandwidth reaches 10.27 GB/sec for large block reads. The server is designed for entry-level computational tasks, lightweight background jobs, low-traffic web microservices, and software testing environments requiring steady, dedicated CPU performance.
